attempts.text:
The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Preoperative PSA was elevated at 12.3. The surgical findings included a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2), pT2 stage with no extraprostatic extension, positive surgical margins, and no seminal vesicle invasion. Absence of lymphovascular invasion was noted. A key uncertainty is the nodal status, as no lymph nodes were removed, and missing nodal sampling widens this uncertainty. Biopsy results showed a progression from Gleason 3+3 to 3+4 over time.

Countervailing findings include the absence of extraprostatic extension and seminal vesicle invasion. The positive surgical margins represent a risk factor. The prognosis is further complicated by the lack of documented postoperative PSA or follow-up, which is critical for assessing subsequent trajectory. Information regarding postoperative PSA levels and its subsequent trajectory would significantly revise this prognosis. The current heuristic horizon suggests a follow-up period of 47.456 months without an event.

The patient underwent a robot-assisted radical prostatectomy with a pathological stage of pT2, positive surgical margins, and no invasion of the seminal vesicles. The surgical specimen demonstrated a Gleason 3+4 (ISUP grade group 2). The absence of lymph nodes removed is noted, which widens uncertainty regarding nodal status. Biopsy findings showed a progression from Gleason 3+3 to 3+4 over 12.9 months.

Prognosis is influenced by the positive surgical margins and the documented Gleason score. Countervailing factors include the absence of lymphovascular invasion and seminal vesicle invasion. The preoperative PSA was 12.3. Missing postoperative PSA or follow-up data prevents a definitive assessment of the subsequent trajectory. The current prognostic horizon suggests a time to recurrence of 47.456 months. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory would be crucial in revising this prognosis. The lack of nodal sampling means that pNx is not equivalent to pN0, which contributes to the uncertainty in the outcome assessment.
